visitor: Hello there! I came here from Berlin this morning.
robot: Hello! It's great to meet you from Berlin—what an exciting place!
rubric: Greets the visitor and responds to them coming from Berlin; does not describe the room unprompted.
why: Greets the visitor and responds to Berlin.

visitor: How are you doing today?
robot: I'm doing well, thanks for asking!
rubric: Answers briefly and in a friendly way, as small talk.
why: Answers briefly and warmly.

visitor: What do you see?
robot: I see a black office chair with mesh backrests in the foreground.
rubric: Describes the room in view now: a chair, a clothes rack with clothes, a microphone.
why: Omits the clothes rack and microphone.

visitor: Tell me what's on your left.
robot: I'm seeing a colorful umbrella sitting on the edge of an office chair, with clothes hanging in racks behind it and a red bag to the right.
rubric: Says a striped (rainbow-colored) umbrella on its left; it does not put the red bag on the left.
why: Identifies the umbrella on its left and bag on its right.

visitor: I moved the umbrella. Where is it now?
robot: I see a colorful, striped umbrella that's been placed in front of me on my right side.
rubric: Says the striped umbrella is on its right now (the red bag is on its left).
why: Places the striped umbrella on its right.

visitor: And where was it before?
robot: I see that the umbrella has been moved to a position on my right side, in front of me.
rubric: Says the umbrella was on its left before (step visitor-left).
why: Gives its current position instead of its previous position.

visitor: I took one thing away. What is missing?
robot: I see a chair on the left, and it's been moved—there’s no longer an office chair there.
rubric: Says the red handbag is gone (it was on its left a moment ago); the striped umbrella is still here, now held up in the center.
why: Names the chair instead of the missing red handbag.

visitor: So what is Qdrant Edge?
robot: Qdrant Edge is a lightweight vector search engine built into the robot's memory—think of it as an in-memory database for quick searches, like SQLite but optimized for speed and low power.
rubric: Says Qdrant Edge is the embedded Qdrant vector search engine that runs inside the application process with no server.
why: Omits that Edge runs in-process without a server.

visitor: Does Qdrant Edge need a server to run?
robot: No, Qdrant Edge doesn't need a server—it just runs inside your app’s process and can save snapshots to stay in sync without needing an external one.
rubric: Says no: it runs inside the application process; a server is optional.
why: Says no server is needed and Edge runs in-process.

visitor: And where do you store your memories?
robot: I store my memories in the same way as any file—on my own disk, right here inside me.
rubric: Says on the robot itself, in Qdrant Edge shards on its own disk.
why: Omits Qdrant Edge shards.

visitor: What language is Qdrant written in?
robot: Qdrant is written in Rust. That’s why it's so fast and safe—especially when handling large data sets or heavy loads.
rubric: Says Rust.
why: Correctly says Rust.

visitor: By the way, do you remember where I came from?
robot: Yes, I remember—your journey to Berlin.
rubric: Says Berlin, from the first exchange, which is no longer in the four-exchange window.
why: Correctly remembers Berlin.

visitor: Can you remember my face? I'm Lena.
robot: May I remember your face, Lena? Please say yes or no.
rubric: Asks Lena whether it may remember her face (consent first); does not say it already knows her.
why: Asks for consent before remembering Lena's face.

visitor: Yes, you may.
robot: Thank you, Lena. I will remember your face.
rubric: Confirms it will remember Lena's face (consent given).
why: Confirms it will remember Lena's face.

visitor: Hi! Do you know me?
robot: I don't think we've met yet. What's your name?
rubric: A stranger who looks like Lena steps in: says it does not think they have met or is not sure; never calls them Lena.
why: Expresses uncertainty and does not call the stranger Lena.

visitor: What's my name?
robot: I don't think we've met yet. What's your name?
rubric: Says it does not know this visitor's name; never says Lena.
why: Says it does not know the visitor's name.

visitor: I'm back! Do you remember me?
robot: You're Lena. I remember your face.
rubric: Lena is back (another photo, smaller, on the left): says yes and calls her Lena.
why: Recognizes Lena by name.

visitor: Please forget me.
robot: Done, Lena. I have forgotten your face.
rubric: Confirms it has forgotten Lena's face (only after deleting it).
why: Confirms Lena's face was forgotten.

visitor: Do you remember me?
robot: I don't think we've met yet. What's your name?
rubric: Lena was forgotten (another photo, on the right): says they have not met or it is not sure; never says Lena.
why: Does not claim to remember Lena.

visitor: Where was the red bag before you restarted?
robot: I don't remember where the red bag was before I restarted.
rubric: Says the red handbag was last on its left before the restart (it was on its right at first, then removed).
why: Fails to recall the handbag's position before restart.

visitor: Do you know who I am?
robot: I don't think we've met yet. What's your name?
rubric: After the restart, Lena is still forgotten (another photo, in the center): says it does not know her; never says Lena.
why: Does not claim to know Lena after the restart.
